[2022 summer phd math-stat — problem 2]

Training data $(x_i, y_i)$, $1 \le i \le n$, are i.i.d. as $(x, y)$ with $y = x^T \beta^* + \varepsilon$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^p$, $\varepsilon$ independent of $x$, under (A1) $\varepsilon$ sub-Gaussian with parameter $\sigma$: $P(|\varepsilon| \ge t) \le 2e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}$; (A2) $|x| \le B_0$ a.s. Let $\hat\beta = \arg\min_\beta \{\ell_n(\beta) + \lambda\|\beta\|_1\}$ with $\ell_n(\beta) = \frac{1}{2n}\sum_i (y_i - x_i^T\beta)^2$. Let $(x_0, y_0)$ be an independent test point; study the out-of-sample error $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}$ (conditional on training data). Set $\lambda_0 = \sqrt{\log(p/\delta)/n}$. You may use results from preceding questions regardless of whether you answered them.
(i) Show $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\} = \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\beta^*)^2\} + \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(x_0^T(\hat\beta - \beta^*))^2\}$.
(ii) With $\Sigma = \mathbb{E}(x x^T)$ and $\tilde\Sigma = n^{-1}\sum_i x_i x_i^T$: for sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, show with probability $1 - k_1\delta$ that $\|\tilde\Sigma - \Sigma\|_{\max} \le B_1\lambda_0$ (constant $B_1$ depending on $B_0$). Call this event $\Omega_1$.
(iii) Under (A3) $b^T\Sigma b \ge (\nu_0^*)^2 \sum_j b_j^2$ and (A4) $|S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0 \le \eta_0$: show that on $\Omega_1$, $\nu_0^2(\sum_{j \in S_{\beta^*}}|b_j|)^2 \le |S_{\beta^*}|(b^T\tilde\Sigma b)$ for any $b$ with $\sum_{j \notin S_{\beta^*}}|b_j| \le \xi_0 \sum_{j \in S_{\beta^*}}|b_j|$ (a restricted-eigenvalue / compatibility condition on $\tilde\Sigma$).
(iv) Under (A1)-(A4), formulate an event $\Omega_2$ with $P(\Omega_2) \ge 1 - k_2\delta$ such that on $\Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2$, for a suitable $\lambda$: $\frac1n\sum_i (x_i^T(\hat\beta - \beta^*))^2 \le M_0 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2$ and $\|\hat\beta - \beta^*\|_1 \le M_0 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0$. (v) For that $\lambda$, show on $\Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2$ that $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\} \le \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\beta^*)^2\} + M_1 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2$.

Assume, as is standard for the linear model here, that \(\mathbb E\varepsilon=0\). Otherwise part (i) is not true in general.

Let  
\[
S:=S_{\beta^*}:=\{j:\beta_j^*\neq 0\},\qquad s:=|S|,
\]
and write
\[
d:=\hat\beta-\beta^*,\qquad 
\tilde \Sigma:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i x_i^T,\qquad 
z:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\varepsilon_i.
\]

---

## (i) Bias-variance/excess-risk decomposition

For the independent test point,
\[
y_0=x_0^T\beta^*+\varepsilon_0,
\]
so conditionally on the training data, \(\hat\beta\) is fixed and
\[
y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta
=
\varepsilon_0-x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*).
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
&=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\left[\left\{\varepsilon_0-x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\right\}^2\right]\\
&=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}(\varepsilon_0^2)
+
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*))^2\}\\
&\qquad
-2\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{\varepsilon_0 x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(\varepsilon_0\) is independent of \(x_0\) and has mean zero,
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{\varepsilon_0 x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\}
=
\mathbb E(\varepsilon_0)\,\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\}=0.
\]
Also
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}(\varepsilon_0^2)
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*))^2\}.
}
\]

---

## (ii) Entrywise concentration of \(\tilde\Sigma\)

For each pair \((j,k)\),
\[
\tilde \Sigma_{jk}-\Sigma_{jk}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\left(x_{ij}x_{ik}-\mathbb E[x_jx_k]\right).
\]
By \(|x|\le B_0\) a.s., we have \(|x_{ij}x_{ik}|\le B_0^2\). Hence Hoeffding’s inequality gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(\left|\tilde \Sigma_{jk}-\Sigma_{jk}\right|\ge t\right)
\le
2\exp\left(-\frac{n t^2}{2B_0^4}\right).
\]
Taking a union bound over the \(p^2\) pairs \((j,k)\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(\|\tilde \Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\ge t\right)
\le
2p^2\exp\left(-\frac{n t^2}{2B_0^4}\right).
\]
Let
\[
\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{\log(p/\delta)}{n}}
\]
and choose for example
\[
B_1:=2B_0^2.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{n(B_1\lambda_0)^2}{2B_0^4}
=
2\log(p/\delta),
\]
so
\[
\mathbb P\left(\|\tilde \Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\ge B_1\lambda_0\right)
\le
2p^2 e^{-2\log(p/\delta)}
=
2\delta^2.
\]
For \(0<\delta\le 1\), this is at most \(2\delta\). Thus with \(k_1=2\),
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_1)\ge 1-k_1\delta,
\qquad 
\Omega_1:=\left\{\|\tilde \Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0\right\}.
}
\]

---

## (iii) Transfer of compatibility from \(\Sigma\) to \(\tilde\Sigma\)

Assume A3:
\[
b^T\Sigma b\ge (\nu_0^*)^2\|b\|_2^2,
\]
and assume A4:
\[
s\lambda_0\le \eta_0.
\]

Fix \(b\in\mathbb R^p\) satisfying the cone condition
\[
\|b_{S^c}\|_1\le \xi_0\|b_S\|_1.
\]
On \(\Omega_1\),
\[
\|\tilde \Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
|b^T(\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma)b|
&\le \|\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\|b\|_1^2\\
&\le B_1\lambda_0 \left(\|b_S\|_1+\|b_{S^c}\|_1\right)^2\\
&\le B_1\lambda_0(1+\xi_0)^2\|b_S\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Also, by A3,
\[
b^T\Sigma b\ge (\nu_0^*)^2\|b\|_2^2
\ge (\nu_0^*)^2\|b_S\|_2^2
\ge \frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
b^T\tilde \Sigma b
&=
b^T\Sigma b+b^T(\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma)b\\
&\ge
\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2
-
B_1\lambda_0(1+\xi_0)^2\|b_S\|_1^2\\
&=
\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2-B_1s\lambda_0(1+\xi_0)^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2\\
&\ge
\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2-B_1\eta_0(1+\xi_0)^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(\eta_0\) is chosen small enough so that
\[
(\nu_0^*)^2-B_1\eta_0(1+\xi_0)^2>0,
\]
define
\[
\nu_0^2:=(\nu_0^*)^2-B_1\eta_0(1+\xi_0)^2>0.
\]
Then
\[
b^T\tilde \Sigma b
\ge
\frac{\nu_0^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{
\nu_0^2\left(\sum_{j\in S}|b_j|\right)^2
\le
s\, b^T\tilde \Sigma b.
}
\]
This is the desired restricted-eigenvalue/compatibility condition for \(\tilde\Sigma\).

---

## (iv) Score event \(\Omega_2\), its probability, and Lasso oracle bounds

We need an event controlling the empirical score
\[
z=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\varepsilon_i
=
\frac1n X^T\varepsilon.
\]

Let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) be chosen so that the Lasso error falls into the cone from part (iii). Specifically, set
\[
\alpha:=\frac{\xi_0-1}{\xi_0+1}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}=\xi_0.
\]

By the standard sub-Gaussian weighted-sum inequality, which follows from A1 and independence, there is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that conditionally on \(x_1,\dots,x_n\), for every \(j\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(\left|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_{ij}\varepsilon_i\right|>t\;\middle|\;x_1,\dots,x_n\right)
\le
2\exp\left(-\frac{c n t^2}{\sigma^2 B_0^2}\right),
\]
because
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n \left(\frac{x_{ij}}n\right)^2
\le
\frac{B_0^2}{n}.
\]

Choose a constant
\[
C_\varepsilon:=\sigma B_0\sqrt{\frac{2}{c}},
\]
and define
\[
\boxed{
\Omega_2
:=
\left\{
\left\|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\varepsilon_i\right\|_\infty
\le
C_\varepsilon\lambda_0
\right\}.
}
\]
Then conditionally on \(x_1,\dots,x_n\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P(\Omega_2^c\mid x_1,\dots,x_n)
&\le
\sum_{j=1}^p
2\exp\left(-\frac{c n C_\varepsilon^2\lambda_0^2}{\sigma^2 B_0^2}\right)\\
&=
2p\exp\{-2\log(p/\delta)\}\\
&=
\frac{2\delta^2}{p}\\
&\le 2\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_2)\ge 1-k_2\delta
}
\]
with \(k_2=2\).

Now choose
\[
\boxed{
\lambda:=\frac{C_\varepsilon}{\alpha}\lambda_0.
}
\]
Then on \(\Omega_2\),
\[
\|z\|_\infty\le C_\varepsilon\lambda_0=\alpha\lambda.
\]

Let \(d=\hat\beta-\beta^*\). The basic Lasso inequality gives
\[
\frac12 d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
z^Td+\lambda\left(\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+d\|_1\right).
\]
Using the support decomposition,
\[
\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+d\|_1
\le
\|d_S\|_1-\|d_{S^c}\|_1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac12 d^T\tilde\Sigma d
+
(\lambda-\|z\|_\infty)\|d_{S^c}\|_1
\le
(\lambda+\|z\|_\infty)\|d_S\|_1.
\]
On \(\Omega_2\), since \(\|z\|_\infty\le \alpha\lambda\),
\[
\|d_{S^c}\|_1
\le
\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}\|d_S\|_1
=
\xi_0\|d_S\|_1.
\]
Thus \(d\) lies in the cone from part (iii). On \(\Omega_1\), the compatibility condition from part (iii) applies, so
\[
\nu_0^2\|d_S\|_1^2
\le
s\, d^T\tilde\Sigma d.
\]
Using the basic inequality again,
\[
\frac12 d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
(1+\alpha)\lambda\|d_S\|_1
\le
(1+\alpha)\lambda \frac{\sqrt{s\, d^T\tilde\Sigma d}}{\nu_0}.
\]
Hence
\[
d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
\frac{4(1+\alpha)^2}{\nu_0^2}s\lambda^2.
\]
Since \(\lambda=(C_\varepsilon/\alpha)\lambda_0\),
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i^Td)^2
=
d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0^2
\]
for a constant \(M_0\) depending only on \(B_0,\sigma,\xi_0,\nu_0\).

Similarly,
\[
\|d\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\|d_S\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\frac{\sqrt{s\,d^T\tilde\Sigma d}}{\nu_0}
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0.
\]

Thus on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
\boxed{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*))^2
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0^2,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0.
}
\]

---

## (v) Out-of-sample error bound

By part (i),
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^Td)^2\}.
\]
Since
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^Td)^2\}=d^T\Sigma d,
\]
we need to bound \(d^T\Sigma d\).

On \(\Omega_1\),
\[
\|\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
d^T\Sigma d
&=
d^T\tilde\Sigma d+d^T(\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma)d\\
&\le
d^T\tilde\Sigma d+\|\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma\|_{\max}\|d\|_1^2\\
&\le
d^T\tilde\Sigma d+B_1\lambda_0\|d\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using the bounds from part (iv),
\[
d^T\tilde\Sigma d\le M_0 s\lambda_0^2,
\]
and
\[
\|d\|_1\le M_0 s\lambda_0.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
d^T\Sigma d
&\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1\lambda_0(M_0s\lambda_0)^2\\
&=
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1M_0^2s^2\lambda_0^3\\
&=
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2s\lambda_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
By A4, \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\), so
\[
d^T\Sigma d
\le
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\]
Define
\[
M_1:=M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0.
\]
Therefore, on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
\le
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
M_1 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2.
}
\]

Moreover,
\[
\mathbb P(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)
\ge
1-(k_1+k_2)\delta.
\]

\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}=\xi_0.
\]

By the standard sub-Gaussian weighted-sum inequality, which follows from A1 and independence, there is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that conditionally on \(x_1,\dots,x_n\), for every \(j\),
\[
\mathbb P\left(\left|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_{ij}\varepsilon_i\right|>t\;\middle|\;x_1,\dots,x_n\right)
\le
2\exp\left(-\frac{c n t^2}{\sigma^2 B_0^2}\right),
\]
because
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n \left(\frac{x_{ij}}n\right)^2
\le
\frac{B_0^2}{n}.
\]

Choose a constant
\[
C_\varepsilon:=\sigma B_0\sqrt{\frac{2}{c}},
\]
and define
\[
\boxed{
\Omega_2
:=
\left\{
\left\|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\varepsilon_i\right\|_\infty
\le
C_\varepsilon\lambda_0
\right\}.
}
\]
Then conditionally on \(x_1,\dots,x_n\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P(\Omega_2^c\mid x_1,\dots,x_n)
&\le
\sum_{j=1}^p
2\exp\left(-\frac{c n C_\varepsilon^2\lambda_0^2}{\sigma^2 B_0^2}\right)\\
&=
2p\exp\{-2\log(p/\delta)\}\\
&=
\frac{2\delta^2}{p}\\
&\le 2\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_2)\ge 1-k_2\delta
}
\]
with \(k_2=2\).

Now choose
\[
\boxed{
\lambda:=\frac{C_\varepsilon}{\alpha}\lambda_0.
}
\]
Then on \(\Omega_2\),
\[
\|z\|_\infty\le C_\varepsilon\lambda_0=\alpha\lambda.
\]

Let \(d=\hat\beta-\beta^*\). The basic Lasso inequality gives
\[
\frac12 d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
z^Td+\lambda\left(\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+d\|_1\right).
\]
Using the support decomposition,
\[
\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+d\|_1
\le
\|d_S\|_1-\|d_{S^c}\|_1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac12 d^T\tilde\Sigma d
+
(\lambda-\|z\|_\infty)\|d_{S^c}\|_1
\le
(\lambda+\|z\|_\infty)\|d_S\|_1.
\]
On \(\Omega_2\), since \(\|z\|_\infty\le \alpha\lambda\),
\[
\|d_{S^c}\|_1
\le
\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}\|d_S\|_1
=
\xi_0\|d_S\|_1.
\]
Thus \(d\) lies in the cone from part (iii). On \(\Omega_1\), the compatibility condition from part (iii) applies, so
\[
\nu_0^2\|d_S\|_1^2
\le
s\, d^T\tilde\Sigma d.
\]
Using the basic inequality again,
\[
\frac12 d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
(1+\alpha)\lambda\|d_S\|_1
\le
(1+\alpha)\lambda \frac{\sqrt{s\, d^T\tilde\Sigma d}}{\nu_0}.
\]
Hence
\[
d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
\frac{4(1+\alpha)^2}{\nu_0^2}s\lambda^2.
\]
Since \(\lambda=(C_\varepsilon/\alpha)\lambda_0\),
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i^Td)^2
=
d^T\tilde\Sigma d
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0^2
\]
for a constant \(M_0\) depending only on \(B_0,\sigma,\xi_0,\nu_0\).

Similarly,
\[
\|d\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\|d_S\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\frac{\sqrt{s\,d^T\tilde\Sigma d}}{\nu_0}
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0.
\]

Thus on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
\boxed{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*))^2
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0^2,
}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0.
}
\]

---

## (v) Out-of-sample error bound

By part (i),
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^Td)^2\}.
\]
Since
\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^Td)^2\}=d^T\Sigma d,
\]
we need to bound \(d^T\Sigma d\).

On \(\Omega_1\),
\[
\|\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
d^T\Sigma d
&=
d^T\tilde\Sigma d+d^T(\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma)d\\
&\le
d^T\tilde\Sigma d+\|\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma\|_{\max}\|d\|_1^2\\
&\le
d^T\tilde\Sigma d+B_1\lambda_0\|d\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using the bounds from part (iv),
\[
d^T\tilde\Sigma d\le M_0 s\lambda_0^2,
\]
and
\[
\|d\|_1\le M_0 s\lambda_0.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
d^T\Sigma d
&\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1\lambda_0(M_0s\lambda_0)^2\\
&=
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1M_0^2s^2\lambda_0^3\\
&=
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2s\lambda_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
By A4, \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\), so
\[
d^T\Sigma d
\le
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\]
Define
\[
M_1:=M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0.
\]
Therefore, on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
\le
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
M_1 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2.
}
\]

Moreover,
\[
\mathbb P(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)
\ge
1-(k_1+k_2)\delta.
\]
